subject: Data retention: what we actually keep (shortlist)
messages:
From: Elena Mendez <elena@brightbank.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Cc: data-privacy@brightbank.com
Date: Fri, 18 Jul 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Quick ask — concise list of what Redwood keeps by default

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks again for the call this morning. BrightBank is reviewing the RFP and we need a very short, precise list for our legal and data-privacy teams: for the hosted Redwood API, by default what items are retained server-side (no custom opt-ins)?

Specifically we need to understand: request inputs (raw prompts), model outputs (complete generations), partial/streamed fragments, KV cache artifacts, and any debug traces or telemetry that could include user content. We also want to know default retention windows and whether there is a straightforward erase-proof we can request.

Could you send a one-page shortlist (bulletized) we can include in the procurement packet?

Appreciate it —
Elena
Data Privacy Lead, BrightBank

Attachment: brightbank_rfi_notes.pdf (summary of their RFP asks)

From: kimberly_park@redwood.ai <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Mendez <elena@brightbank.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 18 Jul 2025 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Quick ask — concise list of what Redwood keeps by default

Elena — thanks for the clear ask and the RFI attachment. Below is a concise, executive-friendly shortlist you can drop into the packet. I kept each item one line and included the default window and opt-out surface where applicable.

Shortlist — Redwood default capture (hosted API, unless customer uses Dedicated/Private):
- Request inputs (user prompts / requests): stored by default for 45 days in the hosted control plane for debugging and quality; customers can opt out or request immediate deletion via account settings or an erasure API for EU/US regions.
- Model outputs (final generations): stored by default for 45 days; same opt-out/erase paths as inputs.
- Streamed fragments (intermediate token fragments during streaming): short-lived buffering only — fragments are persisted temporarily for the session but are not written to long-term logs unless the session completes and final outputs are persisted; default buffer retention is 1 hour.
- KV cache snapshots / runtime caches: treated as ephemeral runtime artifacts; small diagnostic snapshots may be retained for up to 7 days when collected for debugging (only with internal flags enabled); not retained in long-term telemetry by default.
- Debug traces / telemetry (latency, error traces): metadata and anonymized traces are kept by default for 90 days; traces that include full user content are not captured in anonymized telemetry unless explicitly enabled for a debug session.
- Attachments and file uploads: retained according to the same 45-day window unless the customer uploads to a pinned storage bucket (Dedicated/Private) or requests deletion.

Evidence of erasure: we can provide time-stamped deletion receipts for default retention windows and for ad-hoc erasure requests; for Hosted customers this is via the support ticket + audit log export.

Notes / exceptions:
- Enterprise (Dedicated/Private): customers can enforce zero-retention defaults or longer retention via contract and can host artifacts in customer-controlled storage (different defaults).
- EU residency requests: we persist copies only in EU regions when EU residency is selected; default windows remain the same unless contractually amended.

I attached a one-page visual summary (redwood-retention-shortlist.png) and I copied Karthik to confirm procurement wording and any contractual thresholds that BrightBank should request.

If you want, we can convert this into a single bullet to paste into your RFP (single sentence + link to our docs).

—Kimberly
Head of Compliance, Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-retention-shortlist.png (visual), quicklink to RINF-2234 for internal runbook

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, Elena Mendez <elena@brightbank.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 18 Jul 2025 13:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Quick ask — concise list of what Redwood keeps by default

Adding a short procurement-friendly addendum for the RFP:

Procurement-ready language (single short paragraph):
"By default, Redwood stores request inputs and final outputs for 45 days for debugging and quality. Streamed token fragments are buffered during sessions (1 hour default) and not persisted long-term unless the session finalizes. Runtime caches are ephemeral (up to 7 days for diagnostic snapshots). Customers on Dedicated or Private deployments may opt for customer-hosted storage or zero-retention defaults by contract. Deletion receipts and audit exports are available on request."

Contract asks BrightBank may consider:
- Add an optional clause for a 0-day retention for requests/outputs for a subset of production routes (technical vetting required).
- Include SLA for erasure evidence turn-around (we typically commit to 3 business days for hosted customers).
- Specify region residency in the SOW to ensure EU copies are never mirrored to other regions.

I'll leave the sentence-level wording to Kimberly but happy to sign off on the procurement copy.

—Karthik
Director, Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference

From: Elena Mendez <elena@brightbank.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Cc: data-privacy@brightbank.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 18 Jul 2025 16:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Quick ask — concise list of what Redwood keeps by default

Thanks, Kimberly and Karthik — this is exactly the kind of short, actionable language we needed. Couple of clarifying follow-ups before I fold into procurement: 

1) For "deletion receipts and audit exports" — can you confirm the hosted path provides a machine-readable timestamped CSV export with object ids? We need that for our internal evidence capture.
2) Can you confirm the 1-hour buffer for streaming fragments is not accessible via the API after the session ends (i.e., it cannot be reconstituted)?

If we get yes/yes, we'll include the paragraph and request the 3-business-day erasure SLA and the region residency clause. Can you also drop the single procurement paragraph as plain text we can paste into the RFP document?

Best,
Elena
Data Privacy Lead, BrightBank
